T2 is a validity proof of a disclosed verdict (docs/zk.md): it claims no privacy, and no payout in the locked deployment depends on it. It covers the four testnet runs whose content keys are published (fixtures/zk; sealed on chain) and the practice tries the prover service proves.
Fixture bugs are planted textbook classes, labeled in the code; nothing here is a finding in a real protocol.
A mutation score, where shown, measures a rule set's strength, not the code's security.

items.title: Only rule breaks are paid automatically.
items.text: Anything else is at the project's discretion (`top_up`).

items.title: Duplicates are judged by (rule, entry point).
items.text: Two bugs behind one entry point count as one until the first is fixed (rounds).

items.title: One block.
items.text: A proof runs in the anchor block's environment: no time travel, no multi-block attacks.

items.title: Ethereum L1 for verification
items.text: (Sepolia). Other chains are pause and release targets.

items.title: The EVM rules are the manifest's, not the chain's.
items.text: Sepolia runs the Glamsterdam upgrade (its headers carry `blockAccessListHash` and `slotNumber`, and the anchor check hashes them). A proof runs under the rules its manifest commits (`evm_spec: osaka`), so gas is counted by osaka's costs: state creation costs five to seven times more on Sepolia itself.

items.title: Public Sepolia RPCs prove about 128 blocks back
items.text: , so witnesses are built within minutes of an anchor, and the light client runs about 80 blocks behind: a program is created some 15 minutes after its anchor.

items.title: Claims are paid in commit order.
items.text: A commit that is never revealed holds the later ones until its reveal window ends and the keeper expires it (on testnet, a practice try's payout waited ten minutes this way).

items.title: The testnet light client has one trusted relayer.
items.text: Anchors it cannot confirm are labelled project-attested.

items.title: TEE trust is tiered, not removed.
items.text: T1 needs DCAP collateral. Without T1 a verdict rests on OutLayer's operator (T0): under the instant cap it becomes final once its challenge window passes (60 s on testnet), so a false one that nobody challenges stands, and a false Violation is paid; above the cap a second OutLayer run must also agree. A challenge demands T1; anyone may file one, but neither the CLI nor the services do.

items.title: Worker images.
items.text: A worker image OutLayer approves later counts for existing programs only after the image delay (2 days on testnet); until then a run on it gets no T1, so its payout waits the challenge window and its pause waits too, since a pause needs T1 (docs/runbooks/worker-images.md).

items.title: Old anchors.
items.text: A proof that reads beyond the pinned base needs an RPC that keeps the anchor's state.

items.title: Rule strength is the rules' measure,
items.text: and a survivor is not necessarily a bug.

items.title: Testnet only.
items.text: The payout token, wNEAR on testnet, has no value.
